sources.title: Independent edit-operation and metric derivation
sources.details: The minimum edit sequence has unit-cost insertion/deletion/substitution edges. D(i,0)=i and D(0,j)=j; the last step is one of these three operations, so D(i,j)=min(D(i-1,j)+1,D(i,j-1)+1,D(i-1,j-1)+[r_i!=p_j]). Each prefix optimum yields an optimum by induction; the rolling-row code preserves the previous/current rows. Distance is symmetric but CER is not because reference length is fixed. 今天去台北→今天去臺北 needs 台→臺, giving1/5=0.2; corrected-variant omission 今天去臺→今天去臺北 needs insertion北, still1/5; original-variant omission 今天去台 needs replacement and insertion,2/5=0.4. Same Counter does not imply sequence equality: swapped8-codepoint sign has6 minimum edits, so6/8=0.75; removing linebreaks does not restore its order. Mapping both strings台→臺 under a declared policy gives exact equality while raw equality remainsFalse; changing that policy changes the task. Empty reference gives zero denominator, so CER is undefined and presence is measured separately.

sources.title: Independent necessary-context information-loss reasoning
sources.details: In the11.14 construction, each image has32 red and32 blue unit entries in the same8x8 region. The per-channel means are32/64=0.5,0,32/64=0.5 for both, but the opposite order changes64 locations times two channels=128 scalars. Thus two distinct position arrangements map to the same summary, and the summary cannot uniquely determine the order. In11.16, equal Counter values likewise admit distinct character sequences. These counterexamples establish a loss-of-information limit; retaining order does not prove a trained model can understand photos or arbitrary layouts. New context explicitly allows different skill-acquisition routes, while11.16 makes no unique-route or training-quality claim.
